task: Focused repair008: explicit OAuth fragment cleanup failure handling

source_verification.application_change_proof: Exact normalized-text comparison: one shared helper inserted, two original History try/catch statements replaced with calls; all other application text unchanged.

change.behavior: Both recognized OAuth branches use the same cleanup operation. A refused History edit produces generic inline recovery instructions and a native alert; each notice channel has an independent guard.
change.no_navigation: No fallback navigation/reload is introduced. If History refuses the change, the fragment remains and the message says it could not be removed; save/back up before closing and reopening.
change.privacy: Caught History and notice error objects are never logged or interpolated; secondary diagnostic messages are constant strings.
change.preserved: Provider error status, validated auth state, original handled return values, async callback ownership/order, query strings, unrelated hashes and exact tab-only work remain intact.

caller_and_order_evidence.role: Only production caller: window-load redirect completion after draft/pending recovery and session restoration.
Shared cleanup with independent inline/alert failure guards and generic diagnostics.
Error path still reports provider error then returns false; token path still starts validated completion before cleanup and returns the unchanged handled result.

before.meaning: All106 existing auth cases and the ordinary-fragment case passed; three injected History-failure cases kept the URL fragment without a recovery notice.

related_after.scope: Shared cleanup repair before the independent-channel peer adjustment. Recovery/draft functions were unchanged by that adjustment.

tests.peer_case: status-unavailable was added after the original old-app run.
